narrative.intro: Haskell has $262M in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date. Haskell received 9 awards so far this fiscal year, with an average award size of $29.1M. Haskell's obligations are up 582.4% year over year. Department of Homeland Security obligated $226M and Department of Defense obligated $35.8M during FY2026 to date. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction accounts for $262M of Haskell's obligations by NAICS this fiscal year, while Engineering Services accounts for $5K. Historical annual obligations show a rise and fall before the current year: FY21 obligations were $34.3M, FY22 obligations were $54.6M, FY23 obligations were $57.5M, FY24 obligations were $33.4M, and FY25 obligations were $38.3M. The current-year totals are partial because FY2026 to date is a fiscal year to date snapshot. This profile highlights concentration by agency and market for the partial FY2026 period.

sections.heading: Who are Haskell's top federal buyers?
sections.body: Department of Homeland Security is the largest buyer, obligating $226M for FY2026 to date. Department of Defense is the next largest buyer, obligating $35.8M for FY2026 to date. Federal buying is highly concentrated between these two agencies in the current fiscal-year snapshot.

sections.heading: What markets and contract sizes dominate Haskell's federal work?
sections.body: Commercial and Institutional Building Construction is the dominant NAICS, accounting for $262M in FY2026 to date. Engineering Services accounts for $5K in FY2026 to date. Haskell's average award size in FY2026 to date is $29.1M across 9 awards, reflecting larger individual award values this fiscal year.
